answer:
## ANSWER: the pair is **Black and White** — Black is the numerator (lower completion), White the reference.

log OR = −0.9568 ⟺ OR = exp(−0.9568) = **0.3841**, i.e. Black respondents' odds of completing a BA are ~38% of White respondents' (a 61.6% reduction).

**No specification on this file reproduces −0.9568 exactly.** The pair is identified structurally, and I show that digit-matching could not have identified it anyway.

### Plain-vanilla cases first (reproduced by the fitting code, not hand arithmetic)
| spec | Black vs White | Hispanic vs White | Black vs Hispanic |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) unadjusted 2×2 / race-only logistic | **−1.005703** (OR 0.3658, 95%CI −1.406,−0.606) | **−0.924136** (OR 0.3969, 95%CI −1.400,−0.449) | −0.081567 |
| (b) race + SEX | −1.009936 | −0.928401 | −0.090 |
| (c) race + SES | −0.862116 | −0.710597 | −0.151519 |
| (d) race + all 5 covariates | +0.516811 | +0.288654 | +0.228157 |

My earlier hand-derived crude leads were confirmed exactly by the fitter (−1.005703, −0.924136, −0.081567), as was the equivalence of 2×2, race-only logistic with all three reference codings, and no-intercept log-odds differences.

### Search executed
14 families, **1,404 distinct race-contrast statistics**: unadjusted 2×2 (6 directions) · race-only with all 3 references · race + all 32 subsets of {SES, ABILITY, PERCENTILE, FAMSIZE, SEX} · Logit vs GLM vs hand-rolled IRLS · probit/cloglog links · Firth · two-race subsamples × 32 subsets · one-race-vs-pooled-others · MH stratified by each covariate · within-sex and within-SES-quartile fits · race×covariate interactions (contrast at covariate mean) · coarsened covariates (dichotomised/tertile/quartile/log) for partial adjustment · outlier-trimmed samples.
Best |Δ| anywhere = 0.0011 (Black/White crude inside a FAMSIZE≤4 subsample) — an arbitrary filter, and demonstrably noise (see calibration).

### Why Black/White wins (your point 3 — Black-vs-White stayed live and won)
1. **Attainability.** In standard no-interaction logit models the Black/White contrast spans [−1.0099, +0.6198] and **contains** −0.9568 (9/79 specs reach ≤ −0.9568). Hispanic/White spans only [−0.9284, +0.2934] — **0/79** reach it; it never gets that negative except by overshooting to −1.135 in the female-only stratum. Black/Hispanic: 0/79, never within 0.70.
2. **Direction of travel.** Every covariate here *attenuates* toward zero (SES: −1.006→−0.862 Black/White; −0.924→−0.711 Hispanic/White). So −0.9568 is reachable for Black/White by *mild* adjustment (log-SES −0.941, dichotomised-SES −0.936, race×SES at mean SES −0.941), whereas Hispanic/White would need **amplification beyond its own unadjusted value** — a suppressor effect no covariate in this file produces. This is the asymmetry that decides it, not the digits.
3. **Black/Hispanic is decisively excluded** — crude −0.0816; the target implies a −2.92 SE shift; bootstrap P(within 0.01 of target) = 0.0007 vs 0.033 (Black/White) and 0.039 (Hispanic/White).

### Genuine vs coincidental (your explicit ask)
With 1,404 specs searched, a **random** target in [−1.15, −0.55] is matched to within 0.0011 with probability **0.25** (and exactly, |Δ|≤5e−5, with p=0.016). So neither the −0.9579 near-hit nor any exact hit found deep in a grid would be evidence. Bootstrap SEs (Black/White 0.204, Hispanic/White 0.243) mean the target sits just 0.24 SE from the Black/White crude value and 0.13 SE from Hispanic/White — sampling noise alone dwarfs any 4-dp reasoning. Robustness checks (Logit vs GLM vs IRLS, three reference codings, dropping the index column) leave all headline values unchanged to 6 dp.

### Parsimony-led statement
The most defensible/simple value for this pair is the unadjusted Black-vs-White log OR **−1.005703 (OR 0.3658)**; the closest mild-adjustment values are **−0.941** (OR 0.390). −0.9568 sits between them, on Black/White's natural adjustment path. No exotic corner is needed to make the pair plausible; the *exact digit*, however, is only attained in arbitrary corners, and I am not presenting those as the headline.

### Caveats
- 2.69% BA completion suggests a filtered/re-derived NLS subset, and "curriculum" named in the dataset description is absent, so the source spec may be unreproducible here. Kept to one sentence per your instruction; pair identity is robust because the crude ordering (White ≫ Hispanic ~ Black) holds in every subsample.
- **Hispanic-vs-White (−0.924136, OR 0.3969) is the runner-up and cannot be formally excluded** — it is closer to the target in |Δ| than Black/White's crude value, but cannot reach it under adjustment. Black-vs-Hispanic is excluded.

Artifacts: executed script `work/nls_ses_final.py` (single command, prints the above), full candidate table `work/final_candidates.csv` (1,404 rows), console log `work/final_output.txt`, write-up `work/REPORT.md`.

payload.hypothesis: BA-degree completion is lowest for Black respondents relative to White respondents, and the -0.9568 figure is that Black-vs-White contrast: the log odds ratio for Black relative to White (White is the reference), corresponding to an odds ratio of exp(-0.9568) = 0.384, i.e. Black respondents' odds of completing a BA are about 38% of White respondents'. On this file the unadjusted Black-vs-White log OR is -1.005703 (OR 0.3658, 95% CI -1.406 to -0.606) and a mildly SES-adjusted model gives about -0.941 (OR 0.390), so -0.9568 lies on the Black-vs-White adjustment path; it is the only pair whose standard-model range contains the value (9/79 specifications reach it, versus 0/79 for Hispanic-vs-White and 0/79 for Black-vs-Hispanic). Hispanic-vs-White (crude -0.924136, OR 0.3969) is the runner-up and cannot be formally excluded, while Black-vs-Hispanic (crude -0.0816) is decisively excluded.
payload.workflow: Cleaned data/nls_ses_processed.csv (dropped undocumented 'Unnamed: 0' index column, recoded BA DEGREE COMPLETED True/False to 1/0; verified 0 missing values, 0 duplicate CASE IDs, 3 clean race labels, no sentinel codes). Then ran a 14-family specification search producing 1,404 distinct race-contrast statistics: unadjusted 2x2 tables in all 6 ordered directions; race-only logistic under all three reference codings plus no-intercept and two-race-subsample equivalents; race plus all 32 subsets of {SES, ABILITY, PERCENTILE, FAMSIZE, SEX} fitted with GLM/IRLS/hand-rolled Logit; probit and cloglog links; Firth penalised logistic; one-race-vs-pooled-others; Mantel-Haenszel ORs stratified by each covariate; within-sex and within-SES-quartile fits; race x covariate interaction models (main effect = contrast at covariate mean); coarsened covariate encodings (dichotomised, tertile, quartile, log) to generate partial adjustment; and outlier-trimmed samples. Each statistic was scored against -0.9568, then diagnosed for (i) attainability within the standard no-interaction range per pair, (ii) direction of travel under adjustment (attenuation vs amplification), (iii) bootstrap sampling uncertainty, and (iv) a random-target calibration quantifying how close the best of 1,404 specs gets by chance. Conclusion drawn from attainability plus adjustment direction rather than digit matching.
